subject: accountancy
chapter_title: Recording of Transactions II: Cash Book and Ledger

concepts.title: Single Column Cash Book
concepts.definition: A single column cash book records only cash receipts on the debit side and cash payments on the credit side, and the difference between the two totals gives the closing cash balance carried to the next period.
concepts.key_idea: The cash book serves as both a journal and a ledger account, so its balance is found without separate posting.

concepts.title: Double Column Cash Book with Bank Column
concepts.definition: A double column cash book carries cash and bank columns on both sides, records cheques received and deposited, and shows a credit bank balance as bank overdraft when payments exceed deposits.
concepts.key_idea: Contra entries, marked with C, record cash deposited into or withdrawn from the bank and affect both columns without touching the final result.

concepts.title: Petty Cash Book and the Imprest System
concepts.definition: The petty cash book records small repetitive payments under analytical columns such as postage, conveyance and stationery; under the imprest system the petty cashier is reimbursed exactly the amount spent, restoring the float to its fixed amount.
concepts.key_idea: The chief cashier advances the imprest amount, and the petty cashier reports expenses column-wise, which reduces the main cash book's size.

solution_steps.explain: Deduct the petty cash in hand from the imprest amount to get the amount spent
The amount spent is the reimbursement that restores the petty cash to the imprest amount

concepts.title: Posting from the Journal to the Ledger
concepts.definition: Posting transfers journal entries to the ledger accounts of the concerned parties, debiting one account and crediting the other, and each account is balanced to find its net position.
concepts.key_idea: The ledger classifies the chronologically recorded transactions account-wise, and its balances feed the trial balance.

concepts.title: Bank Balance after Deposits and Withdrawals
concepts.definition: The closing bank column balance is obtained by adding deposits to the opening bank balance and deducting cheques issued and payments made, and a negative result indicates a bank overdraft.
concepts.key_idea: This computation mirrors the pass book and prepares the ground for the bank reconciliation statement of the next chapter.

solution_steps.explain: Add the deposits to the opening bank balance and deduct the withdrawals to get the closing bank balance
